history.summary: PROVISIONAL IDENTITY: Map directories list a generic 'Hindu Temple' in Tuensang town (PIN 798612) whose deity is unspecified, alongside a separate 'Assam Rifles Temple' at the Assam Rifles camp. No web source names a distinct Shiva temple in Tuensang. This entry is provisionally linked to the generic Tuensang 'Hindu Temple' listing based on the CSV hint 'Local Hindu shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva'; the deity identification is unconfirmed, and the listing's coordinates are used here. CSV correction: the 'state' column held the town name; the actual state is Nagaland.

name: Shiva Temple
town_description: Tuensang is the headquarters of Tuensang district, the largest district of Nagaland, on the eastern edge of the state bordering Myanmar. A high-altitude hill town in the territory of the Chang, Khiamniungan, Yimkhiung, Sangtam and Phom Naga tribes, known for its ridge-top setting and tribal culture; Indian visitors from outside Nagaland need an Inner Line Permit (ILP).

travel.airport: Nearest airport: Dimapur, then road via Mokokchung (distances approximate; verify locally)
travel.railway: Nearest railhead: Dimapur/Mariani, then road (verify locally)
travel.road: Tuensang is reached by hill road via Mokokchung (NH 202 corridor); the town is approx. 140 km from Mokokchung (verify locally)
